name: Greenhouse
desc: A glasshouse standing in the mid-ground — gable end and receding flank laced with glazing bars on a brick dwarf wall, panes furred with algae and rain-tracks and a few broken clean out — with growth pressed against the inside of the glass, a sun drifting behind the glazing so the bloom crosses pane by pane, and condensation tracking down the inside.

energy.doc: strength of the sun behind the glass, the bloom through it, and the wind on the growth

scale.doc: size of the glasshouse vs frame

density.doc: how many glazing bays and rows the shell is divided into, plus planting and condensation

neglect.doc: algae, grime and rain-tracks on the glass, and how many panes have gone

speed.doc: rate of the sun's drift, the wind and the running condensation

hue.doc: glass hue (176 = cold green horticultural glass; bars and brick answer on the complement)

x.doc: centre of the gable end as a canvas fraction

y.doc: ground line the glasshouse stands on

alpha.doc: opacity of glass, bloom and condensation — the glazing stays translucent at every setting

style.doc: glasshouse: horticultural glass in painted bars, algae in every corner, rain-tracks, lush silhouettes crowding the panes · polytunnel: hooped sheeting instead of glass — matte, sagging, milky, utterly utilitarian · frame: winter — almost every pane gone, the shell reduced to bare structure against the sky, austere and skeletal · prism: the glazing as thin-film interference — each pane a different spectral tint, the whole shell slowly shifting through iridescence, pattern rather than object · sooted: a Victorian house gone to soot and neglect, near-monochrome and grimy, light only getting in where the rain has washed a track

act.doc: drift: an ordinary day, the sun crossing behind the glass · dusk: low warm light, the condensation stops running and the house cools · squall: wind up, the growth thrashing behind the glass

seed.doc: deterministic seed for which panes are broken, algae distribution, and what is growing inside
